newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Moody's rates Westpac floating notes.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates Westpac floating notes.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said it has assigned long term credit ratings of Aaa to the A$591.1 million Series 1997/2 WST Trust Class A Notes to be issued by Westpac Securities Administraion Ltd.
Moody's said the rating is based on the level of subordination provided to the senior notes by the A$13.3 million of Series 1997/2 WST Trust Class B notes, equal to 2.2 percent of total notes issued.
It also reflects the mortgage insurance polices which cover default losses in amount equal to 100 percent of the principal amount of each loan with a loan vaule ratio of over 80 percent or over.

In addition it is based on the pool insurance policy which covers losses on loans with a loan to value ratio of less than 80 percent up to a maximum aggregate default loss on such loans equal to five percent of the total notes issued and also the protection provided to bondholders by a charge over the assets of the Series 1997/2 WST Trust granted to a security trustee.

Moody's said the rating is also based on the quality of the collateral in the form of residential mortgage loans and the strength of the legal documents setting out the obligations of the various parties involved in the programme.
The programme is managed by the Mortgage Corporation Pty Ltd, a 100 percent owned subsidiary of Westpac Banking Corporation, which is rated Aa3 and Prime 1.
